name: The Core
subtitle: Brass · judgment
brief: The castle's bones: the brass pipework that carries everything, and you, from wing to wing. Horns are built from parts (a mouthpiece in, a bell at every open end, valves and slides between). The struggle: judgment, and the judgment you put on yourself. Stand-ins: Brass 01 to 05 (the Atrium and the Cloister).

scenes.title: The Core
scenes.name: The Core
scenes.theme: Judgment, and the judgment you put on yourself
scenes.say: ALL TOGETHER, OR NOT AT ALL. That is the rule. Who made the rule? I made the rule.

scenes.title: The Core: the rooms
scenes.brief: About thirty-five minutes of horn puzzles. Stand-in rooms are real, playable rooms from the prototype dungeon; the wing's other ~20 minutes are uncarved.
notes: Suggested shape for every wing, Nintendo's four steps per mechanic (kishotenketsu): introduce it where it is safe, develop it, twist it, then a room that uses all of it at once.
This is the wing whose mechanics are furthest along: mouthpieces, bells, tees, valves, slides, mutes.

scenes.title: The Pneumatic Line
scenes.say: A brass line from the Undercroft up into the Cloister. Four lanes, sideways.
scenes.brief: Sideways run on all four lanes, the first time you walk from Keys 01 into Brass 04.

scenes.title: The Patchwork Horn
scenes.name: the Patchwork Horn
scenes.say: You found the Patchwork Horn! A horn you can add to: clip on a tube, a valve, a bell, and lock it into the castle's own pipework to finish the horns the castle left half-built.
scenes.brief: Timothy's own scoped instrument: 'a brass horn that you can attach other brass components to, in order to solve puzzles and lock into various structures.' Not built. The horn rules (src/doodads/brass.js) already trace a horn through joined parts, so a carried horn that joins the room's tubes is the natural next mechanic.
notes: The satchel (L to lift, R to turn) already carries drums and reeds; carrying horn parts is the same verb.

scenes.title: The Adjudicator
scenes.name: The Adjudicator
scenes.intro: Order. ORDER. You are about to play. I am about to tell you how it went.
scenes.resolve: That was not what was written. It was... good? I do not have a word for good. I only had words for wrong.
scenes.brief: Judgment as a judge. The hit window narrows and every note gets a verdict (acceptable, sloppy, wrong). In the last phase any lane counts on any note, and the note you choose is the one that sounds: there is nothing left to judge. The game's first rule (no wrong notes) turned into the fight.
notes: Could the judge's comments be the player's own earlier mistakes, replayed?

phases.say: Begin. I will be listening for mistakes. That is all I listen for.
Tighter. Every one on the line. The audience is watching. The audience is me.
...play what you like, then. See if I care.

scenes.title: After the Adjudicator
scenes.brief: A valve that has not turned in years turns. The pipes start to carry again. Tutti relaxes a rule.

shots.say: Somewhere in the walls, a valve turns that has not turned in years. The pipes start to carry again.
You may play in the pipes. Any time. In any order. I have decided that is allowed now.
